short: PR 4959 (tron pull request 4959, the last of four PRs that split PR 4424) keeps the K rows that a short run saves in row-major form inside their own 16-token block of the VNNI-packed K plane (one row of 256 bytes per token), and converts the block to the VNNI layout in place at the end of the forward pass that saved its 16th row. A run of 16 tokens still stores the VNNI layout at once.

In kv_cache.hpp the page records, per storage slot, which rows are saved (k_rows_saved_, one bit per offset) and which blocks are converted (k_vnni_blocks_, one bit per block). Every reader and writer of a row takes the layout from the block bit: set_k_row / get_k_row, the FPGA staging's k_row_if_row_major, the attention path's k_vnni_blocks, the clear path k_forget_row and page copies. Under hardware attention the rows of a short run record no bit, so their block stays row-major.

This page draws the data model, the two layouts of one block, the call graph, the life of one block and the thread timing once (section 1), then shows each of the ten logical changes of the file beside the diagram it alters (section 2).
base_intro: Five diagrams carry the context that every change below refers to. B1 is the data model (book, page, kv_block, the two bit arrays per page), B2 the two byte layouts of one 16-token block, B3 the function model (who calls what), B4 the sequencing model (the life of one block) and B5 the interaction model (which thread touches the state when). The per-change diagrams in section 2 reuse their shapes and colours and say which base diagram they update.
changes_intro: A unit is one logical change: a data model and its helpers, one function's new behaviour, one call path. Each unit shows the head code with its comments (added lines green, removed base lines red, head line numbers in the second column, base line numbers in the first) and, beside it, the diagram that updates a base diagram. Units are ordered by dependency: the design notes (C0), the state (C1), how it is addressed (C2), the read view (C3), who writes the state (C4), the conversion (C5), the row accessors (C6), the whole-block save (C7), the clear path (C8) and page copies (C9).
trivial_intro: Changes that alter no behaviour of the cache and need no picture.
trivial_bullets: Blank separator lines after the new functions (head lines 2184, 2204, 2238, 2248, 2259, 2284, 2373, 2527, 2530, 2538, 2544, 2551, 2565, 2574, 2618: added blank lines) belong to no unit.
The requires(layout_t::uniform_geometry) forwarding overload of note_k_row_saved inside C4 (head lines 2232-2237) only forwards to the primary geometry.
method: The coverage assert of the build (section 5, first bullet) skips blank added lines: the added blank separator lines listed in section 3 sit in no unit or trivial entry.

Thread and ordering facts in the diagrams come from the comments in the diff itself (the new paragraph of Note [K VNNI storage] at head lines 711-761, Note [Row-major blocks under hardware attention] at 763-798, and the function comments) and from the callers' code in model.hpp, self_attention.hpp, full.hpp, gof.hpp and gof.cpp at the PR head 6b081187e1. Every line number was read from the head file. Facts about the earlier PRs of the split (the typed plane of PR 4956, the AMX kernel of PR 4957, the shared window of PR 4958) are drawn as context and cited from the head.

The worked example (page 7, storage slot 5, KV head 0, offsets 0..45 saved, blocks 0 and 1 stored whole, token 37, dimension 70) is an illustration, not a measurement. No performance number appears on this page except the ones quoted from the code comments.

base.title: Data model: book, page, kv_block and the K layout state
base.intro: A book holds one storage slot per layer (plus one EAGLE storage), pages of 64 token offsets, and one kv_block per (slot, KV head, page). The PR adds two atomic bit arrays to the page, one entry per logical slot plus one for the EAGLE storage: k_rows_saved_ (one bit per offset) and k_vnni_blocks_ (one bit per 16-token block). Every arrow says how many. The worked example (page 7, slot 5, offsets 0..45 saved, blocks 0 and 1 stored whole) is the strip at the bottom.

base.title: One 16-token block, two layouts in the same 4 KiB
base.intro: A block owns four 1 KiB panels of its plane. In the row-major form each panel holds four 256-byte token rows (token t of block c in panel (t / 4, c), row t % 4). In the VNNI form each panel holds the 16 dimension pairs of one 32-dimension step for the 16 tokens. block_to_vnni and block_to_rows move a block between the two forms in place. The block bit of the page says which form a block holds.

base.title: Function model: callers, page and book API, k_vnni.hpp operations
base.intro: Each row is one call path through kv_cache.hpp: the caller in another file (with its thread), the page or book function it calls, and the typed operation of h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp that touches the bytes. Every function cell says in one line what the function does and cites its definition. The dashed band lists the new private helpers the rows share.

base.title: Sequencing model: the life of one 16-token block
base.intro: The states of one block of one storage slot, from no row saved to converted, with the operations of this PR as arrows: the decode path row by row (set_k_row, note_k_row_saved, the forward-end conversion), the prefill shortcut (set_k_block, note_k_block_saved), the way back (k_forget_row, page copies) and the hardware-attention branch that records no bits.

base.title: Interaction model: which thread touches the K layout state when
base.intro: One forward pass of one layer and the tree work between passes, one lane per actor: the main thread (the shared window, the row-recording loop, the forward-end conversion), the main helpers (their share of the window), the attention workers (the score readers, the staging gather) and the token tree (clears and page copies under the tree lock). The tinted band is the reader that forces the conversion to wait for the forward end.

units.title: The design notes: the layout state paragraph of Note [K VNNI storage], Note [Row-major blocks under hardware attention], and the consumer list rewritten
lead: Comment text only. It is the design record the code below follows, so it is listed first and shown in full.

The new paragraph of Note [K VNNI storage] (711-761) says: a block holds the VNNI layout only once it is complete and converted. The page records saved rows (k_rows_saved_) and converted blocks (k_vnni_blocks_) per storage slot. Every reader and writer of a row takes the layout from the converted-block bit. Four bullets say who sets, publishes, drops and carries the bits, and why the conversion waits for the forward end (727-734). The last paragraph (754-761) says why the transition is at 16 saved rows.

Note [Row-major blocks under hardware attention] (763-798): when the FPGA scores an operation's K, save_k records no row bits for the rows a short run stores and queues no block. Such a block stays row-major. Whole-block saves still store the VNNI layout and set their bits (784-787). The cost accepted is stated (788-798).

The six consumer items (800-850) are rewritten: item 1 (a run of 16 tokens stores the block whole; any shorter run goes row by row into the row-major tail block), item 2 (the AMX page path needs every block converted), item 3 (the reader scores the VNNI blocks; the row-major tail block takes the dotter), item 4 (the staging reads a row-major row in place), item 5 (page copies carry the bits), item 6 (set_k_row / get_k_row follow the block's layout).

units.title: The K layout state: two bit arrays per page, their helpers, and the state copy
lead: k_rows_saved_ holds one 64-bit word per state entry (one bit per page offset, 2639-2648). k_vnni_blocks_ holds one byte per state entry (one bit per 16-token block, 2649-2653). There are layout_t::n_slots + EAGLE_STORAGE_SLOTS_1 entries. Entry layout_t::n_slots is the EAGLE storage (2520-2529).

Who touches the bits (member comment 2639-2653): row bits are set by save_k (main thread; not for the rows of a hardware-scored operation) and by the full-block save (any thread of a shared window, fetch_or); block bits by the forward-end conversion and the full-block save; both are dropped by clear_kv_complete_at and carried by page copies. A set block bit implies the block's 16 row bits (2651).

k_block_bits(c) is the 16-bit row mask of block c (2539-2543). Its static_assert checks at compile time that page_size == k_vnni::PAGE_TOKENS_64 (one bit per page offset). k_block_is_vnni(state_ix, offset) reads the block bit of an offset's block with acquire order (2545-2550).

The move constructor page(page&&) copies both arrays with relaxed loads and stores, as it already did for kv_saves_ (2022-2027). std::atomic is not movable, and the constructor runs single-threaded, during vector construction (2012-2013).

units.title: Which state entry and which storage slot a call means
lead: book::eagle_view_active says whether the EAGLE view maps logical slot 0 onto the extra physical slot (1135-1138).
k_state_ix picks the state entry of a logical slot: entry layout_t::n_slots for slot 0 while the view is active, the slot's own index otherwise (2531-2537).

k_storage_ref pairs a physical storage offset with its state entry (2193-2196). k_storage_of builds it from a logical slot under the current view (2197-2203). copy_from builds it from the physical slot instead. The deferred conversion list of save_k keeps the resolved pair, so a view change between the save and the forward end cannot redirect the conversion (2185-2192).
k_with_storage_geometry calls a template lambda with the geometry of a storage slot: the slot's declared geometry, or the primary geometry for the EAGLE storage (2552-2564).

units.title: The read view k_vnni_blocks: which blocks of a page hold the VNNI layout
lead: k_vnni_blocks returns the converted-block byte of a slot with an acquire load: bit c set means block c (page offsets 16 c .. 16 c + 15) holds the VNNI layout (2174-2183). It exists for VNNI slots only.

Two readers in self_attention.hpp: k_layout_dense, the third gate of the dense AMX path (the byte must equal BLOCKS_PER_PAGE_MASK_0XF, every block converted, 1915-1928), and the software loop, which marks a token live for k_vnni::qk_group when its block bit is set and scores it with the row-major dotter through row_major_row otherwise (2003-2017).
The removed line at the top of the excerpt is the old one-line comment of set_k_row; its replacement sits at 2285-2287 (unit C6).

units.title: Recording saved rows and whole-block saves
lead: note_k_row_saved sets the row's bit: a relaxed load first, then fetch_or with acq_rel only when the bit is clear (2224-2225). It returns true when the block's 16 row bits are set and its block bit is clear (acquire load, 2227-2229). save_k then queues the block (model.hpp:3426-3428).

Repeat saves: a row saved again into a block that still waits for its conversion returns true again. The conversion is idempotent, so the second queue entry is harmless. A row of a converted block returns false. set_k_row wrote that row into the VNNI column already (2209-2211).
A row-major slot keeps no bits and returns false (2217-2219). The uniform-geometry overload forwards to the primary geometry (2232-2237).

note_k_block_saved publishes the 16 row bits (fetch_or, acq_rel) and then the block bit (fetch_or, release) after a whole-block save (2245-2246). The caller runs it after the last KV head (model.hpp:3333).
Both functions assert their index: offset < page_size (2216), c < page_size / k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16 (2243).

units.title: The in-place conversion of one block
lead: k_block_to_vnni_at loads both bit sets with acquire order (2266-2268). It converts block c of every KV head's plane in place with block_to_vnni (h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp), run through k_with_storage_geometry (2272-2280). It then sets the block bit with a release fetch_or after the last head (2281).

It returns false when the 16 row bits are not all set or the block bit is already set, so a repeated call is harmless (2266-2270). A row-major slot never converts: the lambda's if constexpr leaves converted at false (2273-2279).
Thread rule (2253-2254): main thread only, at a point where no reader of the block runs (the forward end).
k_block_to_vnni resolves a logical slot through k_storage_of first (2255-2258, unit C2).

Callers: convert_pending_k_blocks in model.hpp calls k_block_to_vnni_at with the pair saved at the store (model.hpp:3174). The logical-slot form k_block_to_vnni is called only by tests (t_llama_unit.cpp:2603, t_k_vnni_layout.cpp:598, t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:123).

units.title: Row accessors follow the block's layout: set_k_row, get_k_row, k_row_if_row_major
lead: set_k_row and get_k_row take one token's row as a typed view (const_k_row_view / k_row_view). For a VNNI slot they now branch on k_block_is_vnni (2298, 2341). A set block bit sends them to store_row / load_row (the VNNI column). A clear bit sends them to store_row_major / load_row_major (the row-major tail block). A row-major slot keeps the memcpy (2303-2306, 2346-2349).
The new comment of set_k_row (2285-2287) says the row's saved bit is the caller's (note_k_row_saved, unit C4).

k_row_if_row_major returns the token's row in place for a row-major block and an invalid k_row_view for a converted one (2374-2386). The FPGA staging in full.hpp uses it first and falls back to get_k_row (full.hpp:2757-2762).
None of the three touches the bits.

units.title: set_k_block stores whole blocks only: the present mask is removed
lead: The parameter __mmask16 present is removed (base line 2324). set_k_block now calls store_block with k_vnni::FULL_BLOCK_0XFFFF: the 16 rows of block c of one KV head, stored at once in the VNNI layout (2326-2327).

The comment (2309-2316) says: the result is bit-identical to set_k_row per token of a complete block, only the write pattern differs; the 16 row pointers are native source rows in dimension order; the caller records the block with note_k_block_saved after the last KV head.

Why: a shorter run no longer writes VNNI columns with a masked block save. It goes row by row into the row-major tail block (consumer item 1, 801-812; store_k_block in model.hpp:3297-3300). So the only block save left is the whole one, and the caller asserts present == FULL_BLOCK_0XFFFF before it (model.hpp:3318-3319).

units.title: Forgetting rows when a new token takes an offset
lead: clear_kv_complete_at now also calls k_forget_row(offset) after zeroing the kv_saves_ counters of that offset (2513).

k_forget_row drops, in every state entry, the row bits at and above the offset (mask rows_below) and the block bits of those blocks (mask blocks_below), with fetch_and in release order (2584-2587, 2614-2615). Blocks above the offset hold no live row: their bits are dropped and their bytes are left alone (2580-2581).

Three conditions select the conversion back: the offset's block keeps rows below the offset (block_keeps_rows = offset % 16 != 0, 2587), the block is converted, and the storage is readable. Then the block goes back to row-major first, with block_to_rows for every KV head (2602-2613). So the rows below the offset stay readable.

k_storage_readable holds when no private KV restore is in flight (book.reclaimable_kv_restore_attempt_ == 0) and the page's own chunk has memory (2566-2573). When the storage is not readable only the bits change (2578-2581).

Entries: the EAGLE entry (ix == layout_t::n_slots) ends the loop when the book has no EAGLE storage. Other entries at or above book.logical_slot_count() are skipped (2589-2591). A decode append with nothing at or above the offset costs, per state entry, two acquire loads and no locked read-modify-write (2596-2601).
Thread rule (2581-2582): called with the token tree locked, between forward passes. No reader runs meanwhile.

units.title: Page copies carry the bits with the rows
lead: copy_storage_slot takes a k_storage_ref (unit C2). For a VNNI geometry it asserts count != 0 and loads both pages' bits with acquire order (2735-2741). It computes new_saved once: the destination's bits inside [dst_begin, dst_begin + count) are replaced by the source range's bits, shifted from src_begin to dst_begin (2742-2747).
A whole-page copy (src_begin == 0, dst_begin == 0, count == page_size) is one owner assignment per KV head (dst_block.k = src_block.k) and takes the source's block bits (2760-2762).

Any other range runs three steps per KV head. Step 1: each destination block the range touches whose dst_blocks bit is set goes back to row-major with block_to_rows, and new_blocks drops that bit (2769-2774). Step 2: each row is gathered from a converted source block with load_row, or copied from a row-major one with store_row_major (2775-2784). Step 3: each touched destination block whose 16 row bits are set in new_saved is converted with block_to_vnni, and new_blocks gains that bit (2785-2790).
The bits are stored with release order after the last KV head (2808-2811). The row-major geometry keeps the memcpy per head (2792-2802).
copy_from builds the ref from the physical slot for every active slot and from eagle_storage_offset with state entry layout_t::n_slots for the EAGLE storage (2819-2821, 2828-2831).

glossary: acquire / release (memory orders)

C++ std::memory_order values on the atomic words k_rows_saved_ and k_vnni_blocks_. A release fetch_or (block bit) publishes the plane writes made before it. An acquire load (k_block_is_vnni, k_vnni_blocks) sees them. relaxed carries no ordering (the move constructor). [kv_cache.hpp:2245-2246, 2022-2027]
AMX

Advanced Matrix Extensions, the tile instruction set of the CPU. The AMX QK kernel qk_vnni_128x4 (PR 4957) reads a page's VNNI plane in place as its B operand (the second matrix of the tile multiply). [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:13-16]
attention workers
The threads that consume Q and produce O for the attention jobs. They read a pending page only after every minibatch that writes it counted its latch down. [kv_cache.hpp:731-733]
AVX-512
Advanced Vector Extensions, the CPU's 512-bit vector instruction set. The software reader of VNNI K (k_vnni::qk_group) is AVX-512 code with one token per lane. [kv_cache.hpp:823-825]
bf16 / fp32

bf16 is the 16-bit brain floating-point format of the stored K and V values. fp32 (32-bit float) is the accumulation format of the score kernels. The two readers' fp32 add order differs. [kv_cache.hpp:794-798]
block (16-token block)

Page offsets 16 c .. 16 c + 15 of a plane, 4 KiB. A block holds row-major rows until all 16 rows are saved and it is converted in place. Bit c of k_vnni_blocks_ records the conversion. k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16 = 16, TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 = 4 [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:68-69]. [kv_cache.hpp:711-720]
block_to_vnni / block_to_rows

The in-place conversions of one block in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp (PR 4959): block_to_vnni copies the 16 row-major rows to the stack and stores them as a whole VNNI block; block_to_rows loads the 16 VNNI columns to the stack and stores them row-major. [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:461-491]
book

The struct that owns one KV cache allocation: it reserves space for a requested number of pages and owns the actual memory (a page is a lightweight reference into it). It has n_slots = kv_slot_specs.size() logical slots and owns all DMA memory including the EAGLE storage. [kv_cache.hpp:58-81, 991-997]
cached_operation_uses_hw

model.hpp's per-operation answer, decided once per model, whether the hardware attention scores that operation's K. save_k skips the row-recording loop when it is true. [model.hpp:1529; the skip at 3419]
defrag (book::append)
book::append copies one book's tokens after another's, page by page through copy_from, to defragment books created by tree-shaped speculation. [kv_cache.hpp:1412-1441]
dense AMX path

apply_dense_amx_page: one AMX kernel call for a whole 64-token page. Gates: amx_q_packed != nullptr, is_dense_amx_page (every token relevant through one visible range), and k_layout_dense (page::k_vnni_blocks returns all 4 block bits). Otherwise the page takes the software loop. [self_attention.hpp:1915-1928]
DMA

Direct memory access. The KV books are DMA memory. The allocation itself creates the kv_block objects (Note [KV block lifetime]), so kv_block's members must be trivial to construct and destroy. [kv_cache.hpp:1673-1676, 3021-3024]
dotter

The per-token dot-product loop of self_attention.hpp, struct dotter<T, size> in h/tron/kernels/dotter.hpp (constructed from one query row view). It scores the tokens of a row-major (tail) block through their typed row (row_major_row), 4 lines per token. [kv_cache.hpp:825-828; self_attention.hpp:2011-2016]
dword
4 bytes (DWORD_BYTES_4): one bf16 dimension pair of one token in the VNNI layout. One 64-byte pair row holds 16 dwords (ROW_DWORDS_16), one per token. [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:65, 74]
EAGLE storage view

The book's secondary view for EAGLE (a speculation model). While it is selected (set_storage_view), logical slot zero addresses the extra physical slot. The K layout state keeps one extra entry (layout_t::n_slots) for that storage. [kv_cache.hpp:1135-1138, 2520-2537]
engagement point

The sequence position from which the hardware attention engages: hw_attn_engagement_point() (h/tron/models/hw_attn_config.hpp:22; src/tron/models/hw_attn_config.cpp:42-44), default hardware::MIN_TOK_IDX_FOR_HWATTN = 127 (h/libpos.hpp:90). Below it the software scores the range. [kv_cache.hpp:770-778]
fetch_or / fetch_and

Atomic read-modify-write operations: fetch_or sets bits and fetch_and clears bits in one word, returning the previous value. note_k_row_saved skips the locked fetch_or when the bit is already set [kv_cache.hpp:2224-2225]; k_forget_row's fast path skips both fetch_and calls when nothing is at or above the offset [kv_cache.hpp:2596-2601].
forward end

The end of one forward pass on the main thread, after run() joined the workers and wait_for_coop_gof returned. convert_pending_k_blocks converts the queued blocks there, the first point where no reader of this pass is left. [model.hpp:1834-1842]
GOF
Group-of-four: 4 consecutive tokens of KV data that the staging (gof::populate) copies into a buffer and DMA transfers to the card. [kv_cache.hpp:772-774]
hardware attention

Attention scored by the FPGA (field-programmable gate array) over the K/V it holds. When cached_operation_uses_hw says an operation's K is scored there, save_k records no row bit for the rows a short run stores, and such blocks stay row-major. Whole-block saves still store the VNNI layout and set their bits. [kv_cache.hpp:763-787]
HBM
High Bandwidth Memory, the FPGA device memory. The staging bytes and the HBM layout do not depend on the K layout. [kv_cache.hpp:837-838]
help_drain_gof

The attention workers' share of the cooperative GOF staging: at their between-layer idle point a worker runs pending GOFs from the shared queue (gof::populate and the DMA submit). [model.hpp:3564-3575]
k_rows_saved_ / k_vnni_blocks_

std::array of std::atomic<uint64_t> (one bit per page offset) and of std::atomic<uint8_t> (one bit per 16-token block), each with layout_t::n_slots + EAGLE_STORAGE_SLOTS_1 entries. A set block bit implies the block's 16 row bits. [kv_cache.hpp:2639-2653]
k_storage_ref

A struct of a physical storage offset and the index of its K layout state. k_storage_of(slot) builds it from a logical slot under the current view. copy_from builds it from the physical slot. The deferred conversion list of save_k (pending_k_blocks_) keeps it, so a view change cannot redirect the conversion. [kv_cache.hpp:2185-2203]
k_store_block
model.hpp's name for k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16 = 16: the block length by which save_k cuts a minibatch's tokens into runs, and the item count above which a store is shared. [model.hpp:3150]
kill switch / TRON_AMX_DISABLE

TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 in the environment disables the AMX attention kernels at run time. A TRON_K_VNNI binary then scores VNNI blocks with k_vnni::qk_group. It is an AMX-off run of the same layout, not a rollback to the row-major numerics. [kv_cache.hpp:851-855]
KV head / kv_geometry
One key/value head. kv_geometry holds n_kv_heads and head_size. One kv_block is the KV cache for one KV head in one KV slot of one page. [kv_cache.hpp:108-113, 3010-3013]
KV restore / published / reclaimed storage

Reclaimed storage is the released KV memory of a reclaimable slot. A KV restore allocates it again as a private copy: book.reclaimable_kv_restore_attempt_ is the attempt number while the restore is in flight and 0 again once it ends [kv_cache.hpp:1568]. k_storage_readable is false during a restore and while the page's chunk has no memory; then only the bits change. [kv_cache.hpp:2566-2573, 750-752]
kv_block
The struct holding two planes, K and V, each page_size tokens x head_size dims of bf16. k is either a bf16 array (row-major) or the typed owner k_vnni_tensor (VNNI, PR 4956). [kv_cache.hpp:3010-3027]
kv_saves_
std::array indexed [offset][slot] of std::atomic<uint8_t>: 0 = neither K nor V saved, 1 = one saved, 2 = both saved. The K layout bits are a separate record beside it. [kv_cache.hpp:2634-2637]
latch

A countdown synchronisation object (latch_ref). batch::upstream_kvs_ready is the per-slot latch the downstream attention waits on. save_k_impl counts it down once per downstream minibatch, after all its row stores and marks. [common.hpp:1188; model.hpp:3449]
layout_t (kv_layout)

The compile-time slot table of a book and its pages: kv_layout<slot_specs, ...>, with n_slots = slot_specs.size(), uniform_geometry and primary_geometry. The two K layout state arrays have layout_t::n_slots + 1 entries. [kv_cache.hpp:897-905]
main helpers
Helper threads of the main thread in the generated plugins. The generated run_main_help calls save_k with the helper's worker_ix so they share the K store (PR 4958). [model.hpp:3103-3110]
minibatch / grain

A forward pass processes its tokens in minibatches. A grain is a group of up to 8 speculated tokens (minibatch_grain_size) that is never split across minibatches. A 16-token block may therefore be split across two minibatches of one pass. [model.hpp:199; kv_cache.hpp:727-728]
page

A block of 64 contiguous tokens of KV data (page_size). Attention proceeds page by page. The page struct keeps the per-token, per-slot save counters kv_saves_ and the new K layout bits. [kv_cache.hpp:1994-1996]
page offset

A token's position inside its 64-token page. In the VNNI plane the offset decides the token's block (offset / 16) and column (offset % 16), so copying a token to a different offset moves its bytes. [kv_cache.hpp:2751-2753]
pair row
One 64-byte line = 32 bf16 = 16 dwords: the two values of one dimension pair for each of 16 consecutive tokens. [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:24-32]
panel

One 1 KiB piece of the plane for one 32-dimension step and one 16-token block: 16 dimension-pair rows of 64 bytes in the VNNI form, or 4 token rows of 256 bytes in the row-major form. A VNNI panel is exactly one AMX B tile. [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:29-30, 403-411]
pending_k_block / pending_k_blocks_

One queued conversion {page*, page::k_storage_ref, block} and the std::vector of them in the model. save_k pushes one entry per row that completes a not-yet-converted block (the 16th row bit), and convert_pending_k_blocks drains the vector at the forward end. [model.hpp:3161-3177, 3426-3428]
plane

VNNI (layout)

Vector Neural Network Instructions. In the VNNI layout the two values of a dimension pair of one token are stored side by side. One 64-byte row holds that pair for 16 tokens. It is the B-operand layout of the AMX tile multiply and of the AVX-512 pair dot product. [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:15-20]
work unit / window

batch::k_store_window is the K store window of one shared minibatch (PR 4958): main opens it in save_k, the main helpers join it. Work unit u = items[unit_start[u], unit_start[u + 1]), never crossing a page or a 16-token block. Several units may share one block; each writer touches only its own token's bytes.
